help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Understand how Tatakai works: principles, ranking, and matchmaking.
help.principles.title: Overall principles
help.principles.body:
Tatakai helps you run local tournaments. You record games, and the system keeps track of players, results and ratings.

It does not try to replace your tournament rules. Instead, it gives you a clear view of who played, how often, and how they performed over time.
help.ranking.title: How ranking works
help.ranking.body:
Tatakai uses a rating model inspired by OpenSkill (similar to TrueSkill). Each player has a skill estimate (µ) and an uncertainty (σ).

After each game, ratings are updated based on the teams, their ranks and previous ratings. Players who win against stronger opponents tend to gain more points.

The leaderboard is sorted by a conservative score µ-3σ: this favours players who have both good results and enough games played, while remaining cautious when there is little data.
help.matchmaking.title: How matchmaking works
help.matchmaking.body:
The matchmaking tools help you propose balanced teams for the next game. You choose the candidate players and some parameters (number of teams, max players, bench fairness).

The system then tries to create teams with similar overall strength according to current ratings. It can also rotate who stays on the bench so that everyone plays regularly over time.

You remain in control: the suggested teams are a starting point that you can adjust before saving the game.
